packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-11 - unverified image reading (first reader)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this record. Blind reading.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001, overview, face A)
- Black background, colour checker lower left, cm scale on right edge. Four separate paper(?)/parchment pieces in a row in the lower half:
  (a) a small narrow strip (~x540-590), a few cm tall, written vertically/sideways, with a modern pencil shelfmark-like note;
  (b) a slightly larger narrow strip (~x655-705), also with traces of writing and a modern note;
  (c) a larger fragment (~x840-1110, y615-1060), approx 8 x 13 cm, single column, ~22-23 lines visible, ragged edges, losses at left middle and lower right;
  (d) a second larger fragment (~x1195-1450, y625-1055), similar size, single column, ~22 lines.
- Script on (c) and (d): a cursive German-type current hand (Kurrent-like), brown ink, no ruling visible at overview scale. Interspersed Latin words appear set off in a more upright/roman-style hand (e.g. on (d) a line reading roughly "fecisti faciem tuam d(omi)ne", and on (c) a line with "Sobrii estote"). Tentative interpretation: vernacular prose with embedded Latin citations. Small interlinear additions appear on (d) (e.g. above the "...Gnad ..." line).
- Modern pencil/ink notes (shelfmark-like) are written across (c) near its upper middle and on (d) near the lower part; these are not main text.
- No running titles, rubrics or enlarged initials visible at overview scale.
- Face B presumably in image-008 and its tiles; image-015/016 are small images (strips?).

TILE image-002 (top-left tile of face A: shows top of strip (b) at lower left and the left edge of fragment (c) at right; only line-beginnings of (c) visible here, rest continues in image-003)
Fragment (c), line beginnings (line numbers = order from top of this tile):
002.1  [illegible] ... (top edge, damaged, stained)
002.2  [..]auch de[...]   (or "auch d...")
002.3  er gott [...]
002.4  [..]ch? ihn? [...]   (first word damaged at torn corner)
002.5  Schol[...]  (long s/ascender; continues on 003)
002.6  [..]ist? / [..]ift  (torn area at left)
002.7  er wir? [...]
002.8  Der theil? / Der thail [...]
002.9  will Ach? [...]   (reading uncertain: "will" + capital A-like letter)
002.10 Darkhs? / Dankhs? [...]
002.11 [..]l [...]
002.12 [..]e wo[...]
Strip (b): only two damaged line remains visible: "[..]esp?" / "[..]elber?" - uncertain, likely written across the strip.

TILE image-003 (top-middle tile: upper half of fragment (c), overlaps 002 at left edge; left edge of fragment (d) at far right, read in later tiles). Also viewed contrast crop rscratch/packet-11/c003.jpg (autocontrast greyscale) - modest help only.
Modern pencil note between lines 6 and 7: "STA, Frg. 31-24?" (or "31-2H"; shelfmark-like, not main text).
Hand: German current/Kurrent-type cursive, brown ink, ~11 lines on this tile; letter forms loose, many readings tentative.
Fragment (c), line numbers from top of image-003 (line-initial letters before the [..] are on 002):
003.1  [..] w? es auf [...] [illegible]   (top edge damaged)
003.2  [a]uch der teüfel? (tüfel?) vnd ihre
003.3  [..] gott nit zu tun? (zu kein?) , [..]nd? hein?   (end uncertain)
003.4  [..]ch ahn seiner bildnus? sachen?   (last word uncertain; "bildnus" fairly likely)
003.5  [..]Scholigen? (or "heiligen"?) Vnterthan? oder   (middle word: V + ..th.. + n, uncertain)
003.6  [..]ist: Dem herrn, Amen?   (colon after "ist" visible; last word uncertain, could be "Abra..")
003.7  [..]wir? er seiner Dekret?/Detaro? d[..]   (uncertain)
003.8  [..]t theil so gar seinem [..]t
003.9  [..]ill sich an? [..]heil? nehmen? als   (middle uncertain)
003.10 [..]Darkhs?/Drachs? dann, so will er straffen   (first word uncertain; "so will er strafen" fairly clear)
003.11 [..] wie? dahz?, so nit? in? möglich   (line end "möglich" fairly clear; "so nit in" uncertain)
Overlap note: 002.5-002.12 are the beginnings of 003.5-003.11 (002.5 "Schol" = start of 003.5, 002.8 "Der theil" = 003.8, 002.9 "will Ach" = 003.9 "[w]ill sich", 002.10 "Darkhs" = 003.10).

TILE image-004 (top-right tile: upper half of fragment (d), left margin through right torn edge; contrast crop rscratch/packet-11/c004.jpg also viewed)
Same current hand; Latin line set in a more upright, lighter-weight roman/humanistic-style script.
Fragment (d), line numbers from top of image-004:
004.1  [..]ne? [..]s ersieht? als Goliath [struck/blotted word?] [..]   ("als Goliath" fairly clear; word after it smudged, possibly cancelled)
004.2  [..]macht. Vnd damit?/darumb? wen? künig/kinig [..]   (word after "Vnd" has a heavy flourish, perhaps overwritten)
004.3  [..]s in? grosse? ehr? ware?: hett er g[..]   (colon-like mark after "ware")
004.4  [..]ich würd nit bewegt werden   (umlaut-like strokes over "bewegt"? reading "bewegt" uncertain)
004.5  [..]gy?: Darumb soll mich kein mo[..]
004.6  Da? er aber von seinz? Aug[..]   (first word "Da"/"Der"; "seiner"/"seinz" uncertain)
004.7  gar [struck-through word, ?abwendig] hat er kein? p[..]   (cancellation by horizontal stroke)
004.8  [A]vertisti faciem tuam d(omi)ne et fa[..]   (Latin; "dne" with abbreviation mark; first letter lost at left edge, ascender visible; "Avertisti"/"..vertisti" - first letter only partly seen)
004.9  [..]hast dein angesicht? (angsichten?) von mir abgew[..]   (line end at right edge; "abgew" fairly clear)
004.10 [..]st Gnad [struck word] [interlinear above the struck word: "[..]nädigs?" - reading uncertain] abert?/abwerts?: [struck & underlined word at right] 
004.11 (bottom edge of tile: tops of letters only, read in 007)

       modern pencil note "31 3r"? / "31.3H"? (shelfmark-like) written across between 005b.6 and 005b.7

005b.8 [..]isch? / [..]ifs? (long ascender)

TILE image-006 (bottom-middle tile: lower half of fragment (c) to its right torn edge; left edge of (d) at far right, read later; contrast crop rscratch/packet-11/c006.jpg also viewed)
Fragment (c), line numbers from top of image-006 (line-starts from 005 joined in brackets where the overlap is clear):
006.1  [Darkhs?] dann, so will er straffen   (= 003.10)
006.2  [..]wie? dahz?, so nit in? möglich   (= 003.11)
006.3  [..]lich vnd ewig?/ledig?, vnd erlöss?/erlas? mir?   (line end uncertain)
006.4  [..]ingt?/wegt? alzeit auf dz [..]? kunfft?/künftig? z[..]   (the word after "dz" has a loop-ascender; uncertain)
006.5  [Christ?/Fürst?]liches? ligen?/lügen? der lebe? [..]   (uncertain; the line-start was underlined at left in 005)
006.6  [..]? Sobrii estote &c: Ihr   ("Sobrij estote" in upright Latin script, then "&c:" sign and German "Ihr"/"Ihr")
006.7  [nü?]chtern vnd wachet, der[..]   ("vnd wachet" fairly clear)
006.8  [..]mb? wir ein? A?[..]  (a large initial-like letter then damaged/creased text)
006.9  [C]ui? resiste fortes in [..]   (Latin; "resiste fortes in" fairly clear; "Cui" uncertain, first letters on 005 as "Cti/Cui")
006.10 [..]ber?/[..]hz?: Darumb? in? [..]? [..]   ("darumb" uncertain; rest at damaged lower edge)

TILE image-007 (bottom-right tile: lower half of fragment (d); overlaps 004 at top - 007.1-007.2 = 004.9-004.10)
Modern pencil note across 007.8: "Stams, STA, Frg. 31-1r" (as written on the leaf; shelfmark-like, not main text).
Fragment (d), line numbers from top of image-007:
007.1  [..]hast dein angesicht? von mir abgew[..]   (= 004.9)
007.2  [..]st Gnad [struck word] [interlinear "[..]nädigs?"/"sonders?" above] abert?/abwerts?. [struck & underlined word]   (= 004.10)
007.3  [..]icht gar recht? der weis Man[n?]   ("der weis Man" fairly clear; first word "nicht"?/"sicht"?)
007.4  [..]heit: Der nit?/in? versucht?/verfürt? ist der? [..]   (colon after "-heit"; "versucht" uncertain)
007.5  [..]ein solicher?, spricht? er?, der nit m[..]   ("spricht" uncertain - could be "spaich ich")
007.6  [..]er? feindt?/kennt? seine? böss? ob [..]   (uncertain)
007.7  [..]ig: ob er starckh oder [..]   ("ob er starckh oder" fairly clear)
007.8  [ged?]ultig? &c:   (followed by the modern note)
007.9  [..]sicht?/schreibt? vns gott die zellung?/Lehrung? [..] [..]   ("vns gott die" fairly clear)
007.10 [..]e? ich? wiss? [interlinear/superscript "vn"? or nasal stroke] Vnterschidlich? vn[..]   (uncertain)
007.11 [..]breits?/brecht? Collegi?/Collez? dieser?/diesen? a[..]   (bottom edge, damaged; uncertain)
Limitations for face A tiles: fragment (c) and (d) have line-beginnings lost at left on (d) and line-ends lost at right on (c); many words uncertain because of the fast current hand and abrasion. Strip (a) (smallest) is not covered by any tile I have seen so far on this face; it appears only in overview 001 (not read).

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-008, overview, face B - the reverse sides of the same four pieces, again in a row)
- Same four pieces: (a') smallest strip (~x535-590) with modern note "31-4v?"; (b') narrow strip (~x685-745); (c') larger fragment (~x865-1135) with modern note "Stams, STA, Frg. 31-2v"; (d') larger fragment (~x1190-1455) with modern note "STA Frg. 31-1v?".
- Script: same kind of German current hand, denser and with heavier staining (orange-brown foxing/water stains, pale grey abraded patches) than face A. Single column on each fragment, roughly 22-24 lines. Some words apparently in the upright Latin script (e.g. "...imus" near the bottom of (c')).
- No rubrics or enlarged initials visible at overview scale.
